amendments.because: Narrowed under the owner's Harm 1-2 rule: fixes already stop hard at the commit hook, and keying id-less Jest or Vitest failures by test name is a follow-up; both scored Gain 2, Harm 1
amendments.done_when: When two rounds in a row leave the same failing test or finding, or the change grows past its size limit, Forge stops the item and prints a ready-to-ask question naming the item, what is stuck and what the worker tried, with the choices: switch this item to the other tool, keep the same tool for one more round, or narrow or split; the owner's choice is recorded and the next round follows it

amendments.because: Simplified under the owner's Harm 1-2 rule: matching the same failing test across test runners drew seven review angles (truncated output, mixed runners, id-less lines); two failing rounds in a row is a blunt rule with nothing to parse (Gain 2, Harm 1)
amendments.done_when: When two rounds in a row leave the same failing test (by its test id; for runners without ids, by its failure lines) or the same finding, or a story part grows past its size limit, Forge stops the item and prints a ready-to-ask question naming the item, what is stuck and what the worker tried, with the choices: switch this item to the other tool, keep the same tool for one more round, or narrow or split; the owner's choice is recorded and the next round follows it. A fix past its five-code-file limit keeps the commit hook's existing refusal.

A fix past its five-code-file limit keeps the commit hook's existing refusal.

findings.body: Raise: Not done. For a user-facing item with `tools = "both"` and split workers, a Codex round can be stopped and the owner can choose to switch to Claude. This line selects Claude, but the existing fallback at worker.py:217-228 runs Codex when Claude is unavailable and the checkout is unchanged. The next round therefore uses the tool the owner chose to leave. The named switch proof tests only Claude-to-Codex switching.
findings.title: Not done: switching a design item to Claude can run Codex again

findings.body: Raise: Functional. After round A records a test ID, a round whose failed output contains only a summary takes this return path without clearing `stuck.keys`. If a later round reports A again, Forge counts two and asks the owner, although the two identified A failures were not in consecutive rounds. A normal example is a worker temporarily breaking test collection between two runs of the same test. The summary-only proof starts with no earlier identified failure, so it misses this sequence.
findings.title: Not done: an unidentified failure does not break the consecutive-round count

findings.body: Raise: Not done. The `names or marked` selection discards every Jest, Vitest or unittest failure line whenever the same failing check output also contains one `FAILED ...::...` test ID. A combined repository test command can run both suites: if the ID-bearing failure changes while the same ID-less failure persists, Forge never counts the persistent failure twice or asks the owner. The named proofs run these output formats separately.
findings.title: Not done: mixed test output drops failures without IDs

findings.body: Raise: Not done. `review.test_run` retains only the last 30 ordinary output lines at review.py:397-404. A unittest failure with a traceback longer than that loses its `FAIL: test_a` header while retaining the generic `FAILED (failures=1)` summary. This parser finds no marked failure line, and the guard at close.py:493-498 never counts the same failing test across two rounds. The named unittest proof uses short synthetic output.
findings.title: Not done: long local test output hides repeated failures

stop.reason: Owner rule for Harm 1-2: both round-9 findings are fixed in commit ceaa0d634 (a rerun close with no worker round never counts; unittest FAIL and ERROR lines are keyed one per line), with tests

why: When a worker can't fix a problem or keeps making the change bigger, Forge sends it back round after round and nobody is told
